pullRequests.title: Match nine functions ported from Lombyte (2 executable, 7 level code)
pullRequests.author: Drustburn
pullRequests.head: pr/matches-1
pullRequests.body: Nine functions are now C and match exactly: two in the executable and seven in level code, 17,608 bytes in all. Each is adapted from Lombyte's C for the same function in the US build, with PAL symbols and declared the way this build reaches each global (MACRO_ADDR / SDATA where retail uses the lui macro or $gp). Each replaces its INCLUDE_ASM stub, and the function's staged near miss or functional C is removed with it (nonmatching/functional.tsv and nonmatching/README.md rows included).…

pullRequests.author: Drustburn
pullRequests.head: pr/handwritten-asm
pullRequests.body:
Five functions that are assembly in the original, classified the way docs/ASM_CLASSIFICATION.md does it: listed in config/handwritten_asm.txt / config/overlays/handwritten_asm.txt, their INCLUDE_ASM stub becomes ASM_FUNC, and the report counts them as finished original-source work. ASM_FUNC is INCLUDE_ASM and the same .s is included (tools/organize_asm.py only moves it to asm/handwritten/), so the image is unchanged.
Two of them rest on a kind of evidence the classification has not used yet:…

pullRequests.title: feat(versions): clone changed references; 35 more PAL v1.00 and NTSC-J functions
pullRequests.author: Veradictus
pullRequests.head: feat/versions-clone
pullRequests.body:
Follow-up to #110, all mechanical (no model, nothing written by hand).

tools/version_clone.py now also explains relocated fields that reach another address in the version: a call to a function the release changed or added, a moved table. It renames that symbol in the version's definition only, to the counterpart at that address or a func_<TAG>_/D_<TAG>_ name for code and data only that release has. The checker resolves those names to the version's own address. Candidates are kept only when…
